answer: Continuous lineage tracing ties each identity to a live process it must repeatedly prove by submitting fresh randomness derived from ongoing work—like tending a garden that only grows while watched. Seeds are exchanged with a cedar-coded peer log, and each identity must embed a unique opal marker in its update stream. Duplicates inevitably reuse a marker or desync their lineage, exposing the fork. Attackers pay the full compute and registration overhead per clone, then lose everything when convergence logs reveal the split.
